accuracy.evidence: Facts checked against Polar Bears International species pages, the IUCN Red List account for Ursus maritimus and Stirling's Polar Bears: The Natural History of a Threatened Species: range only around the Arctic Ocean in five countries; blubber over 10 cm thick; black skin under fur whose hairs scatter light rather than being white pigment; paws about 30 cm across used to spread weight and paddle; ringed and bearded seals as main prey; still-hunting at breathing holes as the commonest method; western Hudson Bay ice-free season of about four months (mid-July to mid-November) and several weeks longer than in the 1980s (Stirling and Parkinson 2006; Castro de la Guardia and colleagues 2017). Wet fur losing much of its insulation follows Scholander and colleagues (1950) and Frisch, Øritsland and Krog (1974). The adult text labels the glove times as illustrative, and the paw crack threshold is a model, not a measured value.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common child and adult beliefs about polar bears: living with penguins in the Antarctic (step 1 prediction and feedback, p1, m1, challenge 'south'), fur doing the work in water (step 2 prediction, wet fur result, p2, m9, challenge 'fur'), white skin (m3, challenge 'skin', visual sorter), chasing seals in open water (step 4 prediction and chase button, p3, m5, challenge 'chase'), big paws making the bear lighter (p5, challenge 'light'), and hunting all year in open sea (step 5, m6, challenge 'ice').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpbear is about one species' adaptations and its dependence on sea ice: a blubber glove test with a result chart, a paw-size choice tested on thin ice and in open water, a breathing-hole hunt where waiting succeeds and chasing fails, and a month grid of ice-free time on Hudson Bay. flagpolaran sorts many animals between the poles and compares general adaptations, and flagpengu is about penguin wings, huddles and egg care; neither has glove testing, paw size, still-hunting or a sea-ice calendar. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found by trying it: the polar bear bounces off the Antarctic band, the wet fur bar stops short while blubber runs long, small paws crack the ice and paddle too slowly, the hole without bubbles has no seal and the chase button loses the seal, and tapping a frozen month says the bear can hunt while the four open months show it cannot. The task text afterwards only names what was seen.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong answers the lab disproves: 'Yes, both live where it is icy' (the bear is refused by the Antarctic), 'Thick fur' (the wet fur bar is far shorter than blubber), 'Small, light feet' (small paws crack the ice), and 'It chases them in the water' (chasing loses every seal).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions; wrong options carry six distinct messages naming the slip: wrong pole, wet fur, chasing a faster swimmer, paws making the bear lighter, hunting without sea ice, and white skin; the remaining distractors get a general prompt to recall habitat, warmth and food.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (far north, thick layer of fat, paddles, hole in the ice) and pass the family kid readability limit; the adult text names the Year 1 and 2 programme of study, NGSS K-LS1-1 and 2-LS4-1 and the key terms. Canvas labels are short, and the young layout gives big tiles and 56 px buttons.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: where they live, how they keep warm, what paws do, and how they hunt and what melting ice means. Items cover habitat (p1, m1), blubber (p2, m2, m9), skin (m3), hunting (p3, m5, m8), paws (p5, m7), sea ice (m6) and two counting stories (p4, m4).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android and desktop screenshots in light and dark of every step at the start and after Show me. At 360 px the Arctic and Antarctic bands keep their labels, the three animal tiles sit in one row, the four glove tiles fit with readable names above the tank and the result chart, the five paw sizes and two action tiles fit, the three ice holes and the wait or chase tiles fit, and the 12 months form a 3 by 4 grid. Mouse drags of animals into the bands and of the hand into the tank complete the tasks.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: each animal to north or south, each glove and Dip, each paw size plus Walk and Swim, each hole (the bubbles are named) plus Wait or Chase, and each month. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the result and reason. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
